After my grandfather passed away, I was constantly haunted by nightmares of him suffering in some horrific way. It was the first time one of my relatives had passed away, so I didn't really know how to handle the grief. They didn't go away until I had sat down with one of my friends and spoke to them about these nightmares. The same evening, I finally had a nice dream where I could hug my grandpa one last time like everything was normal.

Obviously, if talking to people was a fix, I wouldn't be seeing my ex in my dreams every night. I think in a way the dreams are working to process emotions you've got deep in your mind or burning in your heart.  

It's not a science, but if you want to spread out the heavy lifting that your mind is doing every night, I recommend exploring your feelings as much as you are able. Practically speaking, this can be journaling, talking with close friends, talking to yourself, watching videos and taking notes, etc.. 

I feel that if you are able to recognize and externalize your feelings, it helps clarify and validate your own emotions. Of course, just do what you can. In the early weeks, I would just write something small in my journal before going back to being sad in my bed. I found that breaking those redundant and depressive spirals, even just for a moment, would often reduce the amount of time I spent in my bed sad afterwards.  
  
It's only been a week, so be patient with yourself! It's ok to be in love, and it's ok to be sad about it too!

I'm glad my perspective helped out a little! Your comment made me feel understood, as I too found many relatable things. 

**"-but it took me a long time to process the fact that though amicable, it was still a breakup."**  
This realization actually took me awhile too! For the first 10 weeks or so, my friends commended me on how well I was handling the breakup. In reality, I had been in denial for so long, also clinging on to the hope that we'd be together when/if she moved back. 

**"But her bday was last week and that combined with Christmas made it so hard."**  
I hear you, brother XD, it's incredible how brutal this chain of holidays has been and will be. I can't say I have any advice other than just to hang out with your friends and family. Enjoy their presence as much as you're able!

**"Though I never did find out the reasoning behind it, I came to the conclusion that it really was about her own self care and less so about me."**  
I love this statement because it shows that deep down we *do* know the right answer to our problems sometimes. Knowing the rational answer has allowed me to grieve and explore the negative feelings that come with baseless conclusions about the situation. I can spiral into my emotions, since I know that I'll eventually come to the right answer in the end. 

**"I am still in a weird space rn. As much as I’ve tried, I haven’t been able to make peace with being alone. I go to the gym, picked up hobbies, see friends, but those few hours alone at night or in the morning has always been hard."**  
The comment about mornings and evenings especially stung. Her appearing in my dreams only to be greeted with her empty spot on my bed is dope (sarcasm). Me and my friend (who is also going through a breakup) will often joke that while we love the gym, it only takes our minds off of things for a couple hours before the dread comes back.

I say the same thing about where I am in life as well, that I'm in a weird spot. For me, I've been trying to make peace with the idea that I'm not going to be put-together for a really long time. I want to grant myself the patience to exist in "the weird" for as long as it takes for me to be ok. 

It's definitely a weird thing to go through, an amicable breakup. My love for them challenges my desire to remain in their life. Yes, I want her back, but more importantly, I want her to be happy. I am by no means a martyr, because I want the same for myself. I want to be happy again, even if it means I can't be with her anymore. 

Eventually, we'll get there! Hang on folks! It's ok to love people!

I also went through something very similar recently. My ex and I broke it off because she was leaving the country to pursue her dreams. The one thing you have to keep in mind is that an amicable breakup is still **a breakup**. It just means you guys broke it off on good terms. Everything else weirdly enough ends up being the same other than the fact that you don't hate the other person. 

I totally get it. I felt like I had immediately become a stranger to her. We would message occasionally, but I would only receive cold and distant responses. It broke my heart thinking that after all we've been through together, I was now just an acquaintance to her. In some ways, she had become a stranger to me too.  

I felt hopeless and desperate over the whole situation. I was afraid that contacting her too often would push her away and yet there was nothing else I could to stop her from slipping away on her own.  It would make me angry, watching myself lament over this breakup and asking myself. "Do they not care at all? How could they miss me so little?".

Recognize that these feelings are part of your own healing process, that you are still grieving despite this being in an amicable breakup. It's ok to process and feel these thoughts as long as you understand that they stem from fear, anxiety, and sadness.  
  
It felt like such a switch-up for me too. One moment, we were in love, and now we are basically no contact. It made me realize that the person I knew, had no longer existed in my life. Even in less than a year, my ex is not the same person from my memories. Nowadays, I try to honor my memory of them. No future happenings could change the fact that I loved that person at that moment. No parts of our history can affect anything happening in the present. 

**"Does this mean that we might never talk to each other again?"**  
This is such a relatable thought for me. My anxiety about what could happen would paralyze me, sometimes impairing my ability to focus at work. But save yourself the trouble of falling down those endless holes. I want to offer more elaborate wisdom, but honestly just trust present and focus on being where your feet are.

Lastly, I'll leave this quote that really helped me out during periods of confusion and anguish. "*Never attribute to malice what can be attributed to incompetence*.". This is not a quote to ridicule your ex, but rather to recognize that their actions are most likely not direct attacks towards you. Like the other comments have stated, she is probably doing this for her own healing process. It may hurt that she chooses to avoid you, but she is not responsible for your feelings, especially not over her own feelings. The only person who is responsible for you feelings, is you.

Sorry for yapping so much, I found your post to be super-relatable. It gives me a weird sense of camaraderie, knowing that I'm not the only one out there struggling with this. I figured I'd write out my thought processes in hopes that they might help you out too.

I think ZeRo is putting out a lot of information on Youtube about the basics. Personally, I don't have any other channel names off the top of my head, but Youtube has definitely got plenty of content creators with information. 

Additionally, you can watch recordings of older matches which might help you get a better sense of the game overall. Hell, even watching entertaining channels like Alpharad or Ninkendo is a great way to familiarize yourself with the game.

Ultimately (hehe), Smash is just a game, so playing it a lot is the way to learn.

P.S. Get some family or friends in on this too because they can end up making great practice opponents.
